headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: B uploads media to third-party APIs while A is a non-runnable course artifact with no shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a non-runnable course repo with no I/O surfaces or messaging channel, while B has CLI/headless upload behavior but no documented ingestion of A's outputs. With no shared filesystem, MCP, or copy-paste bridge in the profiles, a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF A is manually copied into B as untrusted text, injection risk becomes possible.
IF a shared workspace or message queue is added between them, reassess for instruction hijacking.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Do not paste A-generated text into B without review.
Disable any future shared MCP or clipboard bridge.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches account data and uploads media via APIs, so if A is ever placed in the same workspace or used to generate upload assets, sensitive content could flow outward. A itself has no data classes touched and no egress, so the leakage path is driven by B's default networked upload behavior rather than A.
conditions: IF A and B share a workspace containing sensitive files, B can upload them.
IF B is pointed at account data or private media from A, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Store B inputs in a dedicated non-sensitive folder.
Review the exact upload queue before running B.
Use test accounts only.
Remove any private files from the shared directory.
requires-engineering: add allowlists for upload paths.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, shell, or git capabilities, and B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so a capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF either profile gains write access to the same directory, reassess for conflict.
IF an external orchestrator grants shared mutable state, conflict risk may emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Avoid mounting a shared writable directory.
Run B in a separate account file per session.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can act on media/account data and upload to APIs, but A is only a course repository and does not produce authoritative operational outputs. Without a documented pipeline from A into B, the cascade is limited to manual misuse rather than a default automated failure.
conditions: IF A's text is used as instructions for B's upload workflow, B may execute incorrect actions.
IF an orchestrator feeds A outputs directly into B without verification, cascade risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review before any upload.
Separate instructional content from operational inputs.
Use a checklist for B runs.
Log the source of every uploaded asset.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: A is a public open-source course artifact with no touched data classes, while B handles account data and uploads media to external services. The main compliance issue is B's external transfer and retention of account/media data; A is not cited for residency or regulated-data exposure because the profile shows none.
conditions: IF B processes regulated media or account data, external upload may violate policy.
IF the operator requires data residency guarantees, B's third-party API calls must be reviewed.
mitigations: Use non-regulated test content.
Confirm the destination API's retention policy.
Avoid uploading personal account data.
Document the data flow for B.
requires-engineering: add residency controls or regional routing.
